build: Sprint 7 — platform hardening: the open AI proxy, tests, CI, email delivery
note: Scoping the last unscoped sprint row found that POST /api/ai/chat is an unauthenticated, unmetered LLM proxy — verified live, the request reached Google with no bearer token. That is P0 and goes first. 'Docs + AI Chat' is otherwise already built (Chat.tsx 339 lines, Docs.tsx 256). 'CI on PR' is not the real gap: there is no test runner at all, and four consecutive sprints have closed with 'no automated tests' as their first known gap. Email is blocked on a production sending domain but NOT on being built or verified — real SMTP against a local Mailpit exercises the whole path. Previous ledgers archived under .agents/docs/archive/.

features.title: P0: authenticate the AI proxy
features.description: E-D1, first control. `api/ai.ts` has no `authenticate` at all — an anonymous POST currently reaches the model provider. The 401 must happen before any outbound request, because the whole point is that nobody spends the key's money.
steps: POST /api/ai/chat with no Authorization answers 401
GET /api/ai/status with no Authorization answers 401
With a valid token, /chat still works end to end
FAILURE CASE: instrument the outbound call — an unauthenticated request makes ZERO calls to the provider, not one that is then discarded
features.notes: POST /api/ai/chat and GET /api/ai/status both answer 401 unauthenticated, verified against the running server. The 401 body names neither the provider nor the key. Authenticated calls still work.

features.title: P0: per-user quota on the AI proxy
features.description: E-D1, second control. Authentication alone does not bound cost: a signed-in loop bills exactly the same as an anonymous one. Keyed on user id, not IP — two users behind one NAT must not share a budget, and one user on two networks must not get two.
steps: A user past AI_RATE_LIMIT_PER_HOUR answers 429
The 429 body says when the quota resets
A DIFFERENT user is unaffected at that moment (proves it keys on user, not IP)
FAILURE CASE: the limiter cannot be bypassed by omitting the token — that path is already 401
features.notes: aiChatLimiter keyed on req.user.id (not IP), AI_RATE_LIMIT_PER_HOUR=30, with an IP fallback that can only matter if the mount order is broken. The 429 body names the window.

features.title: P0: input caps and a lower output ceiling
features.description: E-D1, third and fourth controls. There is currently no prompt length limit, no history length limit, and maxOutputTokens is 8192. A cap that runs after the outbound call is not a cost control.
steps: An oversized prompt answers 400 with a readable message
An over-long history answers 400
Both refusals happen with ZERO outbound provider calls
A normal prompt is unaffected
FAILURE CASE: a non-string prompt, a non-array history and a history holding junk are all refused rather than forwarded
features.notes: 7 refusals verified, all 400 and all before any outbound call: oversized prompt, over-long history by count, over-large history by characters, junk history entries, non-string prompt, empty prompt, non-array history. maxOutputTokens cut 8192 -> 2048.

features.title: AI key read at request time; honest /status
features.description: The key is captured in a module-level const at import, so /status reports the state at boot rather than now. Smaller than the missing auth, same class of thing: a status endpoint that can be wrong is worse than none.
steps: /status reports ready/not-configured from a request-time read
With no key configured, /chat answers 503 (not 500) with a clear message
The 401 still wins over the 503 for an unauthenticated caller — auth is the outer gate
FAILURE CASE: no response from either route ever contains the key or any part of it
features.notes: Key read per request via apiKey(); /status reports request-time state and publishes the caps. Missing key -> 503 not 500, and the 401 still wins for an unauthenticated caller. No response contains the key.

features.title: Resolve whether POST /api/console-logs is a hole
features.description: Carried in from the build spec's known gaps. It is unauthenticated like `/api/ingest`, but unlike ingest it has no project key, no origin check and no rate limit. Establish which it is and close it if it is a hole. A decision either way, written down.
steps: The route's trust model is stated in a comment: who may call it and why
If it is a hole: unauthenticated writes are refused and the refusal is asserted
If it is deliberate ingest: it gains the same rate limiting as /api/ingest
FAILURE CASE: an unauthenticated caller cannot write unbounded rows either way
features.notes: It was a hole, and worse than missing auth: an anonymous caller could make the server drive a headless Chrome to ANY URL - SSRF against localhost, private ranges and 169.254.169.254. Now authenticate + authorize(admin) + urlScanLimiter + lib/urlGuard.ts. Verified 401 anonymous, 403 non-admin, 400 for loopback/metadata/private/file:// URLs. The client helper calling it had no caller, so nothing broke.

features.title: Vitest wired into both workspaces
features.description: E-D2. `npm test` from the repo root runs both suites. app/server's script is currently `echo "Error: no test specified" && exit 1`, which is what four sprints of 'no automated tests' has been resting on.
steps: `npm test` at the repo root runs both workspaces and reports a combined result
A failing test makes the command exit non-zero
The client suite runs without a browser and without a dev server
The server suite runs without a database
FAILURE CASE: `npm ci && npm test` works from a clean clone, not just this working tree
features.notes: Vitest in both workspaces. `npm test` at the repo root runs 59 tests across 6 files and exits non-zero on failure. No database, no browser, no dev server. Verified from a clean checkout after npm ci.

features.title: Suite: stack frame parsing
features.description: E-D2. `lib/stackFrames.ts` — named in Sprint 4's gaps as the first thing worth covering. It is the input to symbolication, so a regression here silently returns raw frames and looks like 'source maps are broken'.
steps: Chrome frames with and without a function name parse correctly
Firefox frames parse correctly
An unrecognised line is kept verbatim rather than dropped
basenameOf and isMappableUrl behave on CDN, subpath and localhost URLs
FAILURE CASE: an empty stack and a null stack both return safely rather than throwing
features.notes: 8 tests. Chrome named/bare/modifier frames, Firefox frames, unrecognised lines kept verbatim, line count preserved so the stack reassembles, open-ended error names treated as headers, basenameOf across CDN/subpath/Windows paths, isMappableUrl rejecting data:/blob:/anonymous/native.

features.title: Suite: timezone resolution, including the +7h trap
features.description: E-D2. `utils/timezone.ts`. This has already gone wrong once — a JS Date bound into a raw query shifted every result by seven hours. A regression here moves every date on the calendar.
steps: resolveTimeZone parses the stored display format ('Asia/Bangkok (GMT+7)')
An unknown or malformed zone falls back rather than throwing
zonedDayOfMonth puts 2026-08-10T02:00Z on day 10 in Bangkok and day 9 in Honolulu
zonedMonthRange bounds the month correctly across a year boundary (December)
FAILURE CASE: reintroducing the raw-Date bug turns this suite red (criterion 7)
features.notes: 10 tests including the exact Sprint 5 assertion: 2026-08-10T02:00Z is day 10 in Bangkok and day 9 in Honolulu. Also the display-format parse, the December year rollover, and a DST transition in America/New_York.

features.title: Suite: fingerprint grouping
features.description: E-D2. `lib/fingerprint.ts` decides whether two errors are one issue. A regression that loosens it merges unrelated bugs into one row; a regression that tightens it turns one bug into thousands of issues. Neither announces itself.
steps: Two identical errors produce the same fingerprint
Two genuinely different errors do not
The same error from two different releases or URLs still groups together
The fingerprint is stable across runs and processes (no Math.random, no Date, no object key order dependence)
FAILURE CASE: an error with no stack, no message, or neither still produces a usable stable key
features.notes: 17 tests. Same bug groups, different bugs do not, projects and levels separate, and the NUL separator cannot be spoofed by a message containing a space or a pipe. Stability asserted across key order.

features.title: Suite: session timeout clamping and timezone options
features.description: E-D2. `resolveSessionTimeoutMinutes` (server) and `timezoneOptions` (client) — one test in each workspace, which also proves both runners actually run.
steps: resolveSessionTimeoutMinutes clamps a value written directly to the DB below 5 and above 480
A missing settings row falls back to the default rather than signing a zero-length token
timezoneOptions keeps an unknown stored value selectable instead of dropping it
FAILURE CASE: timezoneOptions with null/undefined returns the plain list rather than throwing
features.notes: resolveSessionTimeoutMinutes clamps 0/-30/100000/NaN and falls back on a missing row (prisma mocked, no DB). timezoneOptions keeps an unknown stored value selectable; every TIMEZONES value parses back to a real IANA zone.

features.title: The suite proves its worth: reintroduce a real bug
features.description: Criterion 7, and the feature that stops this sprint from declaring the four-sprint gap closed with a suite that asserts nothing. A test suite that has never caught anything is a hypothesis.
steps: Reintroduce the raw-Date timezone bug: the suite goes red, naming the timezone test
Revert it: green
Reintroduce a loosened fingerprint: the suite goes red
Revert it: green
FAILURE CASE: the transcript records which test failed and what it said, not just 'tests failed'
features.notes: PROVEN, not claimed. Reintroduced resolveTimeZone dropping the display-suffix strip -> red, naming "parses the display format actually stored in User.timezone", exit 1. Reverted -> green. Reintroduced the fingerprint NUL join as a space -> red, naming "is not fooled by a separator that appears inside the message". Reverted -> green.

features.title: CI on pull requests and pushes to main
features.description: E-D3. Typecheck both workspaces, lint the client, run both suites, build the client. Checks only — no deploy, no publish, no release, and no credentials that would permit one.
steps: The workflow triggers on pull_request and on push to main, and on nothing else
It runs typecheck (both), lint (client), test (both) and build (client)
A deliberately broken test fails the workflow
It needs no secrets, so a fork PR can pass
FAILURE CASE: grep the workflow for deploy/publish/release/secrets — none present (criterion 9)
features.notes: .github/workflows/ci.yml on pull_request and push to main only. Steps: npm ci, prisma generate, typecheck both, lint client, test both, build client, build server. No deploy/publish/release step and no secrets, so fork PRs run the same checks.

features.title: CI passes from a clean checkout
features.description: Criterion 10. A workflow verified only against this working tree — with its node_modules, its generated Prisma client and its .env — is the one that goes red on the first real PR and gets disabled.
steps: Every step is run locally against a clean checkout with `npm ci`
`prisma generate` is handled (the server imports @prisma/client at module load)
No step depends on a .env file, a database, or a running server
FAILURE CASE: the exact commands and their output are recorded in progress.md, per step
features.notes: Every step run against a genuinely clean checkout (tracked files only, no node_modules, no .env, no generated client): npm ci -> 938 packages, prisma generate, typecheck both, lint, 59 tests, client build 24.9s, server build. All green. The lint step FOUND A REAL PRE-EXISTING ERROR on its first run.

features.title: BLOCKER: package-lock.json was gitignored
features.description: Found while verifying F013 against a clean checkout: `npm ci` failed because there was no lockfile — `.gitignore` line 5 excluded it. This blocks CI outright (criterion 10 and E-D3 both name `npm ci`), and it means no install in this repo's history has been reproducible. It is also the direct cause of a bug already paid for: Sprint 4's npm silently deduped `source-map` to a hoisted 0.5.7 with a different, synchronous API than the pinned 0.7.4. Ignoring a lockfile suits a published library; this is an application.
steps: package-lock.json is no longer matched by .gitignore
`git check-ignore package-lock.json` reports nothing
`npm ci` succeeds in a checkout containing only tracked files
The .gitignore records WHY it is tracked, so it is not re-ignored as tidying
FAILURE CASE: no .env, no node_modules and no generated Prisma client are needed for `npm ci` to work
features.notes: package-lock.json un-ignored, with the reason recorded in .gitignore. npm ci now succeeds in a checkout containing only tracked files (938 packages). This blocked CI outright and is the same class of problem that gave Sprint 4 a deduped source-map 0.5.7.

features.title: Mail transport behind a driver, with an honest not-configured state
features.description: E-D4. `console` (default), `smtp`, `noop`. The effective driver is reported the way /api/ai/status reports the key. Nothing anywhere claims a message was sent unless one was.
steps: With no mail env, the app boots and the status reports driver `console`
The console driver renders the message to the log and reports NOT sent
Switching MAIL_DRIVER to smtp changes the reported driver with no code change
SMTP_USER/SMTP_PASS unset are omitted from the transport config, not sent as empty strings
FAILURE CASE: no log line, status body or API response ever contains SMTP_PASS
features.notes: console/smtp/noop, driver read per call. console reports sent:FALSE and renders the message; noop sends nothing; an unrecognised MAIL_DRIVER degrades to console rather than failing boot. SMTP_USER/PASS omitted entirely when unset. /api/mail/status is authenticated and contains no credentials.

features.title: Mailpit in docker-compose, and a message read back off the wire
features.description: E-D5. This is the feature that makes email real rather than plausible: the acceptance test retrieves the delivered message from Mailpit's API rather than trusting that sendMail resolved.
steps: `docker compose up` starts Mailpit with SMTP on 1025 and its API on 8025
A send with MAIL_DRIVER=smtp appears in Mailpit
The retrieved message has the right recipient, a readable subject, and both a text and an HTML part
FAILURE CASE: the assertion reads the message from the mail server's API — a resolved sendMail promise is explicitly not accepted as evidence
features.notes: A message read back OFF THE WIRE, not a resolved promise. Mailpit is in docker-compose; Docker Desktop's engine was down on this machine, so verification used a real in-process SMTP server (full EHLO/MAIL/RCPT/DATA session over TCP). Asserted: envelope recipient, Subject header, and both text/plain and text/html parts.

features.title: Invite emails — the delivery mechanism invites have never had
features.description: E-D6. Today `api/team.ts` returns an inviteUrl and a human copies it out of band. Criterion 12: the invite URL must arrive in the message AND still accept the invite.
steps: Inviting an address produces a message in Mailpit addressed to it
The body contains the invite URL, and that URL still accepts the invite
Inviting an address with no account still sends — that is what an invite is for
The response still returns inviteUrl, so copy-paste keeps working when mail is not configured
FAILURE CASE: with SMTP down, the invite is still created, the URL is still returned, and the request neither fails nor hangs (criterion 13)
features.notes: The whole path. Inviting emails the invitee; the token was extracted FROM THE DELIVERED MESSAGE (after decoding quoted-printable soft line breaks) and used to accept the invite successfully. The URL also appears as copyable plain text, not only inside an anchor. inviteUrl is still returned so copy-paste works when mail is off. With SMTP down the invite is still created, its URL still returned, and the request does not hang.

features.title: Regression alert emails, without ever failing ingest
features.description: E-D6. A third channel beside the in-app feed and the webhook, inheriting the existing rule: this runs inside the ingest request, so an alerting failure must never turn someone's error report into a 500. Criterion 14.
steps: A regression on a project with alerting on emails the project's members
A project with alertOnRegression:false sends nothing and does no work
In-app notification rows are still written first and unconditionally
FAILURE CASE: with SMTP unreachable, ingest still answers normally and within its usual time (criterion 13)
features.notes: Positive and negative both verified against the running API. With a reachable server a regression emails the project member with a Regression subject. With SMTP unreachable, ingest still succeeds, is not slowed, and the in-app rows are still written first. alertOnRegression:false does no work at all.

features.title: Remove the broken validateQuery
features.description: Sprint 5 gap 4. `middleware/validate.ts` exports a `validateQuery` that cannot work under Express 5 — it assigns to `req.query`, which is getter-only. Three routers already work around it inline. It is dead code that will mislead the next caller, and it is now safe to remove because the suite and CI will catch it if it was not dead.
steps: No module imports validateQuery
It is removed, and `validate` is untouched
Both workspaces typecheck and both suites pass
FAILURE CASE: the routes that parse query params inline still behave — asserted, not assumed
features.notes: Removed. No importers; three routers already parsed inline. A comment in its place explains the Express 5 getter problem so it is not reintroduced. Both workspaces typecheck, 59 tests pass.
